# Open Video Watermark

> Invisible video watermarking in Python using frequency-domain DCT techniques with REST API and Web UI.

## Overview

Open Video Watermark is an open-source project by Fabrizio Salmi (@fabriziosalmi). It enables embedding imperceptible, compression-resilient watermarks into video frames using Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) in the frequency domain. It features an asynchronous background processing queue, real-time WebSocket progress updates, a modern single-page web UI, and a full RESTful API.

## Core Capabilities

- **DCT Frequency-Domain Watermarking**: Embeds watermarks in the middle frequencies of the luminance (Y) channel of video frames.
- **REST API Endpoints**:
  - `GET /health`: Healthcheck and system status.
  - `POST /upload`: Upload video file and embed invisible watermark.
  - `POST /extract`: Extract embedded watermark bitstream from a video.
  - `GET /files`: List processed files.
  - `GET /download/<filename>`: Download processed video.
  - `DELETE /files/<filename>`: Delete file.
- **WebSocket Streaming**: Frame-by-frame encoding progress emitted via Flask-SocketIO.
- **Production Architecture**: Packaged with Docker, Docker Compose, Gunicorn, and Nginx.

- [Introduction](https://fabriziosalmi.github.io/open-video-watermark/guide/introduction): Architectural overview and DCT theory.
- [Installation & Setup](https://fabriziosalmi.github.io/open-video-watermark/guide/installation): Docker and manual deployment steps.
- [REST API Reference](https://fabriziosalmi.github.io/open-video-watermark/guide/api): Complete API documentation with request and response payloads.
- [Changelog](https://fabriziosalmi.github.io/open-video-watermark/guide/changelog): Version release history and migration notes.
